title: Chuleta de Vaca Tarascada (Braised Beef Chop, Tarascada Style)
description: Prepared with beef, lard, and bacon.

ingredients.name: one well-trimmed and full beef chop
ingredients.sourceText: one well-trimmed and full beef chop

ingredients.name: good broth without fat
ingredients.sourceText: two cups of good broth without fat

ingredients.name: a bouquet of fine herbs and scallions or leeks
ingredients.sourceText: a bouquet of fine herbs and scallions or leeks

ingredients.name: two cloves, minced into one onion of suitable size
ingredients.sourceText: two cloves, minced into one onion of suitable size

steps: Choose a well-trimmed beef chop and have the butcher prepare it, reserving the bone and trimmings for broth
Lard it as if making braised beef and season the surfaces
Tie with twine so it does not lose its shape during cooking
In a braising pan, place bacon slices and ham slices
Place the chop on top, covered with thin bacon slices
Moisten with {{source-6}}
Add six carrots, a bouquet of fine herbs and scallions or leeks, one bay leaf, and two cloves minced into one onion
Place the pan over high heat until it comes to a boil, then cover and continue cooking over low heat for three hours or more, until the meat is very tender
Remove the chop from heat, remove the twine, and keep it warm in some of the cooking broth
Separately, pass the remaining juice through a sieve and reduce over low heat until it reaches a thick consistency
Pour the sauce over the chop, which has been placed on a serving platter

title: Chuleta de Vaca á la Buena Dicha (Beef Chop Good Fortune Style)
description: Prepared with beef.
steps: Brown the beef chop in the butter, turning occasionally so it colors on both sides.
Place the pan over low heat or on a cooktop away from direct flame.
Cover with a lid and place fire on top, renewing it every half hour.
After two hours of cooking, remove the meat from the pan and remove the string.
Place on a serving dish and pour the degreased cooking juice over the top.

title: Chuleta de Vaca á la Real (Beef Chop Royal Style)
description: Prepared with beef, veal, and broth.

ingredients.name: 1 veal hand, deboned and cut into four pieces
ingredients.sourceText: 1 veal hand, deboned and cut into four pieces

steps: Have the butcher remove the bones from the end chops, keeping only the bone from the middle chop with its attached piece of meat.
Prepare, lard, season and tie the meat as described in previous formulas.
Place in a braising pan with the veal shoulder, veal hand cut into four pieces, and concentrated broth.
After two hours of cooking, add the carrots cut lengthwise into equal pieces.
Continue cooking for two to three more hours until the meat is very well done.
Remove from the pan and remove the string.
Place on a serving dish, arranging a row of small onions browned and colored in beef butter around it, and another row of carrots cooked at the same time.
Pass the strained, degreased and reduced juice through a sieve and pour over the meat and vegetables at serving time.

description: Prepared with veal, butter or lard, and bread.
steps: Sauté six well-prepared chops in a pan, without breading them, in 125 grams of butter or lard.

title: Chuletas de Ternera à la Amorosa (Veal Chops in the Loving Style)
description: Prepared with veal, lard, and bacon.
steps: Beat the veal chops slightly and flour them, one by one, evenly.
In a pan, for twelve chops, melt one ounce of lard with three tablespoons of very good oil, some bacon scrapings and ham bits.
Sauté the chops over high heat, and when they have taken on a good color and are well browned, moisten them with two glasses of Malaga, Marsala, or Alicante wine, or any sweet wine.
Let it cook over low heat until the wine is consumed, and then season and add broth or a little juice to bathe the meat.
At the moment of serving, remove the chops, which are placed on a plate over croutons of equal shape, and pour over them the sauce that is in the pan, straining and sifting it through fine linen.

title: Chuletas de Ternera à la Milanesa (Veal Chops Milanese)
description: Prepared with veal, melted butter, and bread.
steps: Prepare six good veal chops and soak them in melted butter so that they take the grated bread well mixed with salt and pepper.
Beat six eggs, and in the beaten egg dip the already breaded chops, and immediately bread them again with grated bread mixed with Parmesan cheese.
It is necessary to insist on this second breading so that the chops are covered with the greatest amount of grating.
Melt 250 grams of very fresh butter and fry the chops in it, which should take on a very good color.

description: Prepared with chops and meat.

ingredients.name: two chops together, each with two ribs
ingredients.sourceText: two chops together, each with two ribs

Fill the hollow in the middle with a finely chopped meat filling from meatballs, and join the two parts of the meat of the chops together again, and roast on the grill until they are well done.

title: Chuletas de Ternera á la Antigua Española (Veal Chops Old Spanish Style)
description: Prepared with veal and butter or oil.
steps: Allow the piece of meat from which the chops are to be cut to age, then remove the large bone from the end, the skin, the tendons, and the fat if desired.
Flatten with a mallet or iron or wooden plank, and round them with a knife, cleaning the bone or rib of the muscular meat, leaving only the end bare for easy gripping.

Roast on the grills a little, then stew in a pan with butter or oil, as preferred and convenient, or leave them on the grills so they reach their proper point of cooking and can be presented at the table.

title: Chuletas Verdes de Cerdo (Green Pork Chops)
description: Prepared with pork chops, lemon juice, and shallots.
steps: In a bowl or tureen, macerate in lemon juice for six hours a good amount of chopped parsley, two tarragon leaves finely chopped, and half a dozen shallots, with salt, pepper, cloves and nutmeg.
After that time, grill the chops on a grill grate over high heat.
Little by little incorporate the fat that the chops release into the bowl and mix it with the marinade, which is thickened and bound with toasted and grated bread.
At the moment of serving, place the chops on a very hot platter and coat them on both sides so that the meat is not visible with this paste garnish, using a spatula for this.

Despite the precaution of heating the platter, the time spent in the operation and the garnish that is cold will cool the chops; to serve them hot after being prepared, put them in the oven with the door open or cover them with a cloche cover with fire on top.

title: Chupe (Lamb and Potato Stew-Soup)
description: A soup made with lamb, onion, and lard.

ingredients.name: lamb leg, cut into very small pieces, cleaned of fat, tendons and skin
ingredients.sourceText: Two pounds of lamb leg, cut into very small pieces, cleaned of fat, tendons and skin

ingredients.name: One large onion the size of an egg, finely chopped
ingredients.sourceText: One large onion the size of an egg, finely chopped

ingredients.name: Potatoes, cut into pieces the size of coins
ingredients.sourceText: Potatoes, cut into pieces the size of coins

steps: Put a liter of water to boil in a pot and at the first boil, add two pounds of lamb leg cut into very small pieces, cleaned of fat, tendons and skin.
Cook the meat over slow and steady heat for three hours, without needing to skim the broth.
Season and add a little oregano, one large onion the size of an egg finely chopped, half a tablespoon of paprika, and one heaping tablespoon of lard.
Continue cooking the broth for a quarter hour.
Thirty minutes before serving the dish, which with these quantities is calculated for six people, add potatoes cut into pieces the size of coins.
This stew-soup must be very brothy, so care should be taken during cooking, and if the broth reduces or is consumed, add water before seasoning.
Serve with a spoon.

title: Civet de Liebre (Hare Civet)
description: Prepared with hare, butter or lard, and bacon.

ingredients.name: one and a half quarts good red wine
ingredients.sourceText: one and a half quarts good red wine

ingredients.name: two dozen small onions the size of walnuts
ingredients.sourceText: two dozen small onions the size of walnuts

steps: Make a dark roux or brown sauce with {{source-0}} and one tablespoon flour.
In this roux, sauté and brown 125 grams bacon shavings.
Add the quartered hare pieces to the pan and brown them over high heat to firm the meat.
Pour one and a half quarts of good red wine into the pan, ensuring all hare pieces are well covered.
Add a bouquet of fine herbs, two dozen trimmed mushrooms, two bay leaves, salt and pepper.
Cook over high heat so the sauce reduces violently by at least two-thirds.
When the hare is cooked, add two dozen small onions previously sautéed separately in lard.
From that point, let the civet rest by the fire without cooking, keeping it very hot for serving.
Minutes before serving, add triangular croutons to the dish, well soaked in the sauce, to garnish the platter.

When the hare is cooked, add two dozen small onions previously sautéed separately in lard.
From that point, let the civet rest by the fire without cooking, keeping it very hot for serving.
Minutes before serving, add triangular croutons to the dish, well soaked in the sauce, to garnish the platter.

title: Codornices a la Vitoriana (Quail Vitoria Style)
description: Prepared with quail, broth or water, and white wine.
steps: Clean the quail well and remove the legs, head and wings.
Pierce the thighs with small sticks or reeds from one side to the other.
Place them in a cooking pot with butter and add broth or water.
Remove and split them lengthwise down the middle.
Remove the small bones and fry again in butter with a little hot broth or water.
Make the pastry dough with one and a half pounds of flour, one pound of fresh cow butter and one glass of white wine at the start, the rest water.
Work the dough well so it is not hard. After working it well, place the butter in the middle of the dough, extend it a little and then fold the dough over it, doing this three times.
Cut one round piece for the base and then one long strip; moisten it slightly with a feather in water and place it around the edge.
Cut another round piece for the lid and place it in a well-heated oven with heat above and below, moistening it from time to time with butter on top.
As it begins to cook, cut off the lid and remove the middle leaves and let it cook more. When it reaches the right point, remove it.

title: Codornices Asadas (Roasted Quail)
description: Prepared with quail, bread crumbs, and egg yolks.
steps: After cleaning, turn the quail on the roasting spit.
Have a pot on the fire with butter from cows, in which you will add salt, some bread crumbs, a pinch of pepper, and one egg yolk for every two quail.
With some feathers, brush the quail repeatedly with this mixture until they are well browned.
Alternatively, roast them slowly and wrapped in grape leaves, and serve with whatever sauce is most pleasing to the diner.

title: Codornices á la Jardinera (Quail Gardener's Style)
description: Prepared with quail, broth or meat or juice, and butter.

ingredients.name: four to six types of legumes
ingredients.sourceText: four to six types of legumes

steps: Prepare, truss, and bridle the quail.
Brown them over strong fire in butter from cows.
Moisten with a quarter of a measure of water and let them cook at low fire for half an hour.
Separately, cook four to six different types of legumes.
In a baking dish, arrange the quail on large croutons, forming a star with heads grouped in the center.
Fill the spaces between them with cooked legumes, combining types and colors.
When the dish is well decorated, pour broth from the pot or concentrated meat juice.
Bake in the oven at gentle fire for a quarter of an hour.

title: Col Rellena (Stuffed Cabbage)
description: Prepared with cabbage, sausage, and chestnuts.
steps: Scald a Lombard or white headed cabbage in boiling water. Open the leaves slightly without deforming the vegetable and carefully remove the heart.

Prepare a filling of ground sausage meat with an equal quantity of roasted and chopped chestnuts, a bouquet of fine herbs, and good seasoning of salt and pepper. Place this filling in the hollow left by the heart.
Tie the cabbage with kitchen twine and cover the filling with a slice of bacon.
Place the cabbage in a braising pot or casserole in which there is a good wide slice of bacon. Around it place carrots and onions studded with whole cloves.
Cover completely with broth from the pot and cook over gentle heat. Place the cabbage on a serving platter.
Strain the sauce and reduce it by half, adding 115 grams of fresh cow butter and 1 tablespoon of potato starch.
Once the sauce is bound, pour it over the cabbage.

title: Coliflor en Salsa Blanca (Cauliflower in White Sauce)
description: A sauce made with cauliflower, white sauce, and salt.
steps: Boil salted water in a large pot, and when it boils vigorously, add the cauliflower well washed in several waters and divided into florets that form the head.
Cook for a quarter hour. Remove and let drain. To prevent it from cooling, place it in a casserole without covering it, near the fire.

Prepare the white sauce and bind it in a small casserole. Take the cooked cauliflower pieces one by one and arrange them in an enameled earthenware soup tureen with the florets facing down and tightly packed.

Take a silver or white metal platter of equal size but not as deep, which is to be used for serving the dish, place it as a cover over the tureen and turn it over so that the cauliflower appears whole on the serving platter.
Pour the sauce over the top.

title: Compota de Camuesas (Camuesa Apple Compote)
description: Prepared with apples, syrup, and juice.
steps: Cut camuesas in half, removing the cores and seeds.

Peel them, taking care that they remain of equal size, and place 8 deciliters of syrup at 16 degrees in a saucepan with a capacity of 2 liters, adding the juice of half a lemon to cook all this slowly.
When the camuesas are cooked, drain them in a strainer, and then strain the syrup, which is reduced to 32 degrees.
Once the camuesas are completely cold, arrange them in the compote dish, one in the middle and the rest around it, and sprinkle with the syrup.

title: Compota de Castañas á la Vainilla (Chestnut Compote with Vanilla)
description: Prepared with chestnuts, sugar syrup, and vanilla pod.
steps: Remove the shells from four dozen beautiful chestnuts and place them in fresh water

Place them on the fire in a pot with capacity of two liters with one and a half liters of water, and blanch them; that is, remove the inner skin or peel, and place them in a pan, avoiding that some rest on top of others
Cover with syrup at 16 degrees, and then make the mixture tremble over the fire, just barely, for just under half an hour
When the chestnuts are cooked, drain them in a sieve
Strain the syrup through a chinois strainer and reduce it to 30 degrees
Arrange the chestnuts in the compote dish and water them with the syrup
To the chestnut compote, made as just described, add one-quarter of a vanilla pod

title: Compota de Peras de Invierno (Winter Pear Compote)
description: Prepared with pears, syrup, and vanilla.

ingredients.name: 5, 7, or 9 beautiful winter pears of equal size
ingredients.sourceText: 5, 7, or 9 beautiful winter pears of equal size

steps: Select 5, 7, or 9 beautiful winter pears of equal size, as much as possible, and peel them, taking care that they remain very smooth and avoiding letting the knife leave marks.
Place them in a saucepan with a capacity of 2 liters and cover them with syrup at 16 degrees, to which add 1 teaspoon of vegetable carmine and 1/4 of a vanilla stick.
Boil very gently until they are completely cooked, which is tested by seeing if the pears yield to finger pressure, and let the pears cool in the syrup.
Drain them and reduce the syrup over high heat until it reaches 32 degrees.
Place one pear in the middle of the compote dish and the other 4, 6, or 8 around it, and pour the syrup, which should be cold, over them.

steps: First thing to do is sauté the whole rabbit in cow or pork butter and let it cool

If the rabbit is very tender, it will be good to wrap it in a sheet of greased paper so it cooks without drying out
Remove the paper halfway through cooking so it browns, moistening it frequently with its own juices
Serve the roast rabbit alone on a platter, and apart in a sauce boat, its own juice, reinforced with a spicy sauce

title: Conejo Salteado según Gouffé (Rabbit Sautéed, Gouffé Method)
description: Prepared with rabbit, white wine, and broth.
steps: Clean and gut the rabbit and cut it into pieces.
Place in a flat sauté pan: {{source-1}}, {{source-2}}, 1 pinch nutmeg, 2 pinches of mixed spices, 2 pinches salt, and 2 pinches pepper.
When the butter is melted, place the rabbit pieces in the sauté pan over high heat for twenty minutes.
After this time, remove the rabbit and place on a serving dish.
In the same pan add 25 grams of flour, stirring circularly over the fire for one minute.
Add two deciliters of white wine and one deciliter of broth.
Bring to a boil for five minutes, then strain the sauce through a chinois strainer.
Clean the sauté pan and return the sauce and rabbit to it.
Add 20 grams of chopped small onions, well washed, and 1 tablespoon of chopped parsley.
Bring to a boil and serve at the first boil in the sauce.
Do not cook further as boiling hardens them after the first boil.
If necessary, the rabbit can be sautéed in an ordinary pan over the flame, proceeding the same way but taking care to constantly sauté the rabbit so it cooks evenly.

title: Congrio (Conger Eel)

steps: Purchase a piece of conger eel of one kilogram; if the piece contains intestines, be careful to remove them
Wash and tie it as you would meat for a stew, then blanch for a quarter hour in boiling water
Remove from water, drain and place in a pot with a capacity of four liters, which will be filled with water in such a way that it well covers the fish
Add the onion cut into thin slices or strips of half a centimeter, parsley sprigs, 2 bay leaves, 2 deciliters of vinegar, 1 garlic clove, 30 grams of salt, 20 grams of peppercorns
Cook very gently for half an hour, drain and serve on a platter over a napkin, garnishing it with parsley
Serve separately in a sauce boat either white sauce or hollandaise sauce, or better yet melted butter

description: Prepared with artichokes, water, and salt.
steps: Cut off the tips and trim the leaves of the artichokes
Boil in plenty of water with plenty of salt, as with all green vegetables
When the liquid boils vigorously, cook until pulling a leaf from an artichoke causes it to separate immediately
Place in a colander on a plate
When they can be squeezed slightly with the fingers without burning, drain them well so they release the water
If they are to be eaten only cooked, place them in the oven with the door open or on the edge of the stove to dry slightly and not cool

title: Crema de Café (Coffee Cream)
description: Prepared with coffee, egg yolks, and water.
steps: In a saucepan, bring one quarter litre of water to a boil; when it boils vigorously, add {{source-1}} and stir well with a spoon, putting it back over the fire until it increases in volume four or five times over the vessel.
Let it rest to settle clearly, without straining and mixing it with an equal quantity of milk and sugar, and cook everything again so that it reduces a little.
In a pan, dissolve very well with a little flour powder five egg yolks, which are stretched with the milk and coffee, until the mixture is perfect.
Then pass this through a sieve.
In a deep serving dish or in caramelized molds on the inside, set the cream to curdle in a water bath.

title: Crema de Chantilly (Chantilly Cream)
description: Prepared with cream, powdered sugar, and maraschino or rum or liqueur.

ingredients.name: four quartillos of good fresh cream
ingredients.sourceText: four quartillos of good fresh cream

ingredients.name: one spoonful of gum tragacanth powder
ingredients.sourceText: one spoonful of gum tragacanth powder

ingredients.name: two small glasses of maraschino, rum, or another good liqueur
ingredients.sourceText: two small glasses of maraschino, rum, or another good liqueur

steps: Pour four quartillos of good fresh cream into a porcelain bowl with one spoonful of gum tragacanth powder.
Place the bowl over crushed ice and beat the cream well with a wire whisk.
As thick, compact foam forms, remove it with a skimmer and place it in a sieve to drain, continuing this same operation until no more foam remains.
After it has drained well, place it in another clean bowl.
Add the powdered sugar as needed.
Before serving at the table, add two small glasses of maraschino, rum, or any other good liqueur.
This cream is placed on a serving dish, over a fine pastry tart or in a timbal formed with sponge cakes.
It can also be flavored with vanilla by grinding it with piloncillo sugar; with chocolate by dissolving one ounce in half a glass of boiling water; with orange or lemon by scraping the zests.

title: Eggs of Any Desired Size (Huevos del Tamaño que se Quiera)
description: Prepared with eggs.

ingredients.name: Multiple eggs, quantity depending on desired size
ingredients.sourceText: Multiple eggs, quantity depending on desired size

steps: Break as many eggs as desired, more or less depending on the size desired for the final egg.
Separate the yolks from the whites when breaking them.
Take a very clean bladder whose capacity can hold all the yolks and fill it with them after they have been well beaten.
Tie the bladder very well to prevent air from entering and suspend it in boiling water until the yolks have taken on a suitable consistency.
Untie the string of the bladder and remove a giant yolk.
Then take a larger bladder, place the beaten egg whites in it, place the yolk in the middle, and tie it again.
Expose everything to the heat of boiling water until the enormous white has hardened enough that the final bladder can be broken and release the enormously large egg.

description: Prepared with ham, pork, and eggs.

ingredients.name: Very fine slices of raw ham
ingredients.sourceText: Very fine slices of raw ham

steps: Beat the egg whites separately and keep the yolks, two by two, in small bowls.
In a round baking dish or pan at least twenty centimeters in diameter, line the bottom completely with very fine slices of raw ham.
Add pork lard on top and place the pan on strong heat over a griddle, preferably not over a small stove.
When the fat begins to sizzle, pour all the beaten egg whites over it, and as soon as they set, add the yolks one by one.
Sprinkle with salt, pepper, and finely chopped dried parsley.
Serve as an appetizer course.

title: Ensalada Conferencia (Conference Salad)
description: A salad made with potatoes, mustard, and onion.

ingredients.name: six lettuce heads for the leaves
ingredients.sourceText: six lettuce heads for the leaves

steps: Hard boil six eggs and steam one kilogram of potatoes

Two hours before eating, mash the eggs in a large salad bowl with salt, pepper, mustard, clove, nutmeg with parsley, tarragon and onion in sufficient quantity, mixing with one tablespoon of good vinegar
Add six tablespoons of oil, and in this thick sauce add the potatoes and mix, stirring for a long time
Cover everything with the leaves of six lettuce heads, well washed and dried
At the moment of eating, add vinegar that should be strong and in quantity half the amount of oil
Shake and mix well, stir vigorously and eat

title: Ensalada Francillon (Francillon Salad)
description: A salad made with potatoes, broth, and vinegar.

ingredients.name: two glasses of Bordeaux white wine, Iquem brand
ingredients.sourceText: two glasses of Bordeaux white wine, Iquem brand

steps: Cook potatoes in broth and slice them
While still warm, season with salt and pepper, refined oil and aromatic vinegar from Orleans
Add two glasses of Bordeaux white wine, Iquem brand, and finely chopped parsley, chervil and aromatic herbs
Cook sea dates in broth with a celery stalk, cleaned well of filaments
Mix everything together, first removing the shellfish from their shells, combining with the seasoned potatoes, stirring slowly with two spatulas
The proportion of sea dates to potatoes should be one third less, so that the shellfish flavor is barely perceptible
Once the salad is well mixed and tossed, cover the domed surface with slices of truffles cooked in Champagne wine
Make this salad two hours before serving so it is completely cold

title: Entrecote Ángel Maro (Angel Maro Entrecote)
description: Prepared with steak or meat and pork.

ingredients.name: One substantial entrecote steak, meat aged four days in winter or two days in summer
ingredients.sourceText: One substantial entrecote steak, meat aged four days in winter or two days in summer

steps: Have a very hot fire ready.
Strike the entrecote on both sides with a boxwood mallet on a wooden cutting board, then clean it and remove all attached fats, skin, nerves, and tendons.
Trim the meat so that only uniform, solid meat remains, with no trace of anything else—this is the secret to success.
Put enough pork lard in a pan so that when melted, the entrecote can be submerged two or three times without the fat stewing or startling it, but only to completely impregnate it with lard.
Remove the entrecote from the pan with an iron fork, holding it suspended in the air so the fat drips onto a plate.
Empty most of the fat from the pan, leaving it only lightly greased, and place it on very hot fire until the small amount of remaining lard crackles.
Using the same fork, place the entrecote in the pan, shaking the pan slightly.
After two or three minutes, small air bubbles will appear on the surface of the meat and burst. Then sprinkle the entrecote with ground salt—nothing but salt—and turn it over.
The same bubbling effect appears on the second surface, and complete the seasoning with another dusting of salt.
Remove the pan far from the fire and cover it hermetically with a fitted lid and weight on top.
After five minutes, serve it alone on a very hot plate.
Before cutting the entrecote, you will see it bathed in abundant juice according to this method, and the meat will be as tender as sponge cake.

title: Entrecote á la Parisiense (Ribeye Steak Parisian Style)
description: Prepared with steak, beef, and salt.

ingredients.name: 1 entrecote (ribey steak), 15 centimeters long and 6-7 centimeters wide
ingredients.sourceText: 1 entrecote (ribey steak), 15 centimeters long and 6-7 centimeters wide

steps: Flatten the meat by striking it on its edge (thickness) and refine and shape the edges with a knife.
Soak the raw meat in melted beef butter.
Over high heat, sear and cook directly on the cooktop, turning to cook the other side when the first side is done.
Place on a serving dish with a touch of beef butter kneaded with finely chopped parsley, salt and a touch of pepper.
Before serving, mark the meat with three or four lines using a heated poker from the stove to simulate the toasted marks of grill grates.
Serve with fried potatoes or other elegant potato preparations.

title: Epigrama de Cordero (Lamb Epigram)
description: Prepared with lamb, bacon, and beef.

ingredients.name: Breadcrumb coating well salted and peppered
ingredients.sourceText: Breadcrumb coating well salted and peppered

steps: Separate the shoulder blade and debone it completely.
Lard it with thin strips of bacon and season with salt, pepper and fine herbs.
Tie and secure it well in a rounded form that bulges on one side.
Braise it in a pot with a trace of beef butter and a ladleful of broth.

Continue quartering what remains of the half lamb: the ribcage, the breast, the flank, the hind quarter, etc., and cook all of it together in the juice and seasoning of the shoulder blade, which will already be braised.
When cooking is finished, strain the sauce, degrease it and reduce it if it is clear.
Allow the ribcage and shoulder blade to cool, but compress them beforehand between two pot lids so they do not deform as they cool.
Once cold, pass and repass them through melted and lukewarm beef butter and coat them with finely grated breadcrumb well salted and peppered, giving them color on the grill over a strong fire.
Separately, sauté the small chops as described for mutton, and roast on a spit the leg and all the pieces already prepared.

Place the shoulder blade, removing the string, in the center of a serving dish, and arrange all the other pieces around it, making the difference of each piece of meat and its special seasoning evident to the eye.
Pour over the dish thus arranged the sauce from the cooking, which can be increased with meat juice, incorporating in all cases lemon juice.
Serve this dish very hot.

title: Escorzonera con Salsa Blanca (Black Salsify with White Sauce)
description: A sauce made with salsify, white sauce, and vinegar.

ingredients.name: finely chopped beef kidney fat
ingredients.sourceText: 100 grams of finely chopped beef kidney fat

steps: Place the salsify in a pot with 2 liters of water and 2 tablespoons of vinegar
Cut the heads off the salsify and scrape them completely to remove the black skin, placing them in the water as they are scraped
Put {{source-3}} in a 3-liter pot and melt it without browning
Add 2 liters of water, salt, and 2 tablespoons of vinegar
Stir over high heat until the first boil
Put the salsify in the pot and cover, leaving a 4-centimeter opening
Cook very gently for half an hour at the side of the stove
Drain and cut into 7-centimeter pieces
Place in a 2-liter pot, cover with white sauce, and serve

title: Espárragos Cocidos (Cooked Asparagus)
description: Prepared with asparagus, salt, and water.
steps: Gather asparagus into a bundle without untying it, and cut all the stems together at once so that all the ends are equal, leaving them at a length three times that of the edible part.
Untie the bundle, scrape the non-edible extremities, wash very well, and arrange them neatly in a package on the removable bottom of an asparagus cooker box, securing them with a few turns of twine.
Place the asparagus cooker box full of water over high heat so that the asparagus submerges well.
Add a little salt, and when the water boils vigorously, place the asparagus inside and cook for twelve minutes.

Remove the asparagus, cut the twine from the removable bottom, and place them on a silver or metal tray whose flat part or bottom is covered with one or two well-pressed napkins, leaving the edges of the tray uncovered.

Arrange the asparagus on the tray with care and skill in two bundles, with the tips of the two bundles touching each other, so that the diner may easily serve themselves by taking them with their own left hand and with the aid of a small spatula in the right hand.
Serve with a sauce of choice, accompanied by a double-spouted gravy boat of the same metal, with its saucer in one piece.

Place the prepared meat in a braising pot with the deboned veal hand, a bouquet of fine herbs, and one large onion in which two or three cloves are studded

title: Extracto de Caldo de Vaca en Pastillas (Portable Beef Broth Extract in Tablets)
description: A soup made with veal, beef or meat, and mutton.

ingredients.name: beef or cow meat
ingredients.sourceText: Six pounds of beef or cow meat

ingredients.name: One and a half pounds of veal top
ingredients.sourceText: One and a half pounds of veal top

steps: Place all ingredients in an earthenware pot and cook with low heat in sufficient water.
Skim carefully and strain the broth, pressing it well.
Boil a second time with fresh water, strain again, and let both broths cool to remove the fat.
Combine the two broths.
Strain and evaporate in a double boiler until it has the consistency of paste.
Remove from the vessel and spread on marble stone.
Cut into small tablets and finish drying in a double boiler or oven until brittle.
Store in a glass bottle sealed with cork, sealed with wax, and kept in a dry place.
To use: dissolve half an ounce or 15 grams of these tablets in water, add a little salt, heat over gentle heat, and serve or use in making soups.

Thin and bind with the broth from cooking.

title: Fricando (Braised Veal)
description: Prepared with veal, bacon, and broth.

ingredients.name: a piece of veal shoulder, about three pounds
ingredients.sourceText: a piece of veal shoulder, about three pounds

steps: Debone and lard a piece of veal shoulder of three pounds with thin strips of bacon.
Place the meat in a braising pan with two deciliters of broth.
Put on the heat and let it boil until the broth is reduced, preventing the meat from sticking to the bottom of the pan.
When the juice of the meat takes on a yellowish tint and becomes consistent and gummy, add another six deciliters of broth.
Let it cook very gently for one hour and a quarter with very slow boiling, the pan half covered with its lid.
After this time of slow cooking, remove the lid and replace with a flat iron lid with a shovelful of coals on top.
Baste the veal every four minutes until a yellowish and shiny tint appears; this operation serves to concentrate.
Arrange the meat in the serving dish.
Strain the juice through a chinois strainer; decrease it and pour it over the piece of veal.
Place the sorrel puree in the serving dish first; the piece of veal on the sorrel and baste with the juice.

Cut carefully the meat and skin adhered to the bones and remove them so that all the inside comes out and only the meat and skin remain

Cook in water with onions, carrots, garlic, thyme and parsley until done

title: Gibelota de Conejo (Rabbit Stew)
description: Prepared with rabbit, beef or pork or lard, and bacon.

ingredients.name: bacon, cut into small squares
ingredients.sourceText: 125 grams bacon, cut into small squares

steps: Prepare the rabbit and quarter it as shown on page 443.
Brown it well in 125 grams of beef or pork lard and equal quantity of bacon cut into small squares.
When the bacon is very golden, remove it from the pot, and in the same fat, brown the rabbit pieces until the meat becomes firm and toasted.
Set aside the browned rabbit on a plate.
In the same pot with the same fat, toast a heaping tablespoon of flour, and moisten with two ladles of broth and the same amount of white wine.
Immediately incorporate into the pot the bacon pieces and rabbit pieces that were set aside.
Add trimmed mushrooms and cook over high heat.
When the gibelota lacks only a quarter of the cooking time, season with salt, pepper, a bouquet of fine herbs, and two dozen small onions that have been previously browned in pork lard.
Manage the cooking so that the sauce is thick and reduced when the rabbit is cooked through.
Serve very hot.

title: Glaseado (Brown Glaze Sauce)
description: A sauce made with chickens, kidney, and carrots.

ingredients.name: calf kidney fat
ingredients.sourceText: three pounds of calf kidney fat

ingredients.name: two large onions with cloves inserted
ingredients.sourceText: two large onions with cloves inserted

steps: Place the two chickens, calf kidney fat, carrots, onions with cloves, concentrated broth, and bouquet of fine herbs in a pot.
The important point in preparing the glaze is that the meats do not stick to the pot and do not take on color.
When the juice begins to thicken, moisten with a little consumed broth and add gradually, little by little, until it well bathes the meats.
Prick the meat at once with a knife so that it releases its juice, and let it cook over low heat.
Prepare separately a white roux with flour, in which cook a good handful of well-cleaned mushrooms, cut up and seasoned beforehand in the cold with salt and lemon juice.
Mix the white roux with the broth in which the meats are cooking.
Continue cooking everything for two hours.
Skim and degrease and strain through a metal mesh strainer.
If the preparation is done well, the glaze will result white.

description: Prepared with bacon, ham, and onions.

ingredients.name: a heaping spoonful of pork lard
ingredients.sourceText: a heaping spoonful of pork lard

ingredients.name: roasted meat juice from the previous evening
ingredients.sourceText: roasted meat juice from the previous evening

steps: Fill the bottom of a casserole with thin slices of bacon, and on top, as a second layer, place very thin slices of Trevélez ham.
Trim twelve onions the size of apples into slices, and use them to cover the ham and bacon.
When the onions have cooked almost over brisk heat, remove and set aside the ham and bacon.
Add a heaping spoonful of pork lard, stir the onion in the casserole with a spatula, lower the heat and take care that it does not brown.
Season well and add roasted meat juice from the previous evening to a small pot of broth, then bind with a dissolved egg yolk and a thread of vinegar.
This onion garnish serves for all kinds of dishes, and can be presented as a platter at family tables with the ham and bacon, though these should be saved for other uses.

title: Gubios Fritos (Fried Gudgeon)
description: Prepared with fish, flour, and oil.
steps: Scale the gudgeons and gut them
Clean and dry with a fine cloth without washing
Place in a napkin and sprinkle flour over them
Gather the four corners of the napkin as if making a bundle and shake the fish to coat thoroughly with flour
Let rest in the napkin for half an hour until the fish's moisture has made the flour adhere well
Flour again with fresh flour
In a large pan holding four pounds of oil, fry about thirty gudgeons the size and thickness of a finger over high heat to perfection
Do not fry more quantity at once in the same oil, nor fry thirty gudgeons in less fat, as this will spoil the operation
When well fried, the gudgeons are eaten in their entirety including head, bones, and flesh

Let rest in the napkin for half an hour until the fish's moisture has made the flour adhere well
Flour again with fresh flour
In a large pan holding four pounds of oil, fry about thirty gudgeons the size and thickness of a finger over high heat to perfection
Do not fry more quantity at once in the same oil, nor fry thirty gudgeons in less fat, as this will spoil the operation

title: Guisado Blanco de Ternera (White Veal Stew)
description: Prepared with veal, butter or lard, and broth.

ingredients.name: one ladle of cream or two of milk
ingredients.sourceText: one ladle of cream or two of milk

steps: In a saucepan, brown two tablespoons of flour in butter or lard, and moisten with one ladle of clear broth and another of cream, or in its absence, two of milk.
In this sauce, seasoned slightly, place the pieces of veal to warm, but without allowing them to cook.
Separately, cook mushrooms and very small onions in clear broth; season with salt and pepper and incorporate into the meat.
When serving this white stew, bind it with three egg yolks dissolved in water, so that the stew becomes creamy and slightly yellowish.
Make sure the sauce is not too thin, resulting in a dish fit for a good table, and more than leftovers, a variant of any of the white veal stews.

title: Guisado Blanco de Ternera (White Veal Stew)
description: Prepared with veal, butter or pork, and broth or water.

steps: Cut the veal breast into pieces the size of chocolate ounces.
Pass the veal pieces in cow or pork butter without letting them brown. Remove them with a skimmer and set aside on a plate.
In the same butter, without letting it take on color either, brown two tablespoons of flour.

Immediately moisten with broth or water, and when the sauce is thickened and somewhat thin, incorporate the veal pieces that were set aside all at once, along with about two dozen large onions the size of walnuts, an equal number of small mushrooms or champignons, and the same quantity of pitted olives.
Cook everything over low heat until the sauce reduces and becomes like a paste.
Half an hour before serving, season with salt and pepper, and sprinkle with a good tablespoon of dried parsley powder.
Away from the heat, with the dish already in a covered serving bowl, bind the sauce with one egg yolk dissolved in a couple of tablespoons of water.

title: Huevo Frito (Fried Egg)
description: Prepared with egg and oil or lard.
steps: Break the egg, putting the white in one cup and the yolk in another
Lightly agitate the white without beating it
Place the pan over high heat
Heat the liquid (oil or lard) until it produces a thin vapor with a brownish color, turning into the characteristic blue smoke of fats when boiling begins
At this moment, remove the pan from the heat
Pour the white in a thin stream from a hand's breadth of height, as if decanting
Immediately and without losing time, with great speed, throw the yolk into the middle of the white
Cover the pan and after three minutes remove the lid and take out the fried egg, placing it on the plate in which it is to be eaten
Do not add salt; the consumer should add it to their taste

title: Huevos Amerengados (Meringue Eggs)
description: Prepared with eggs, powdered sugar, and orange.

ingredients.name: six eggs (separated into whites and yolks)

steps: Separate the whites from the yolks of six eggs.
Beat the whites to stiff peaks and add salt with 30 grams of powdered sugar, {{source-3}}, and continue beating so that the mixture combines well.
Apart, over low heat, reduce by a quarter one liter of cream, in which the peel of one lemon with one hundred grams of sugar and {{source-7}} will have been added.
If there is no cream, substitute with two liters of milk, which will be reduced by half, cooking it very slowly.
When the milk is boiling, the beaten whites are added successively in portions with a small ladle, so that they have a spherical form.
Turn the balls in the milk so they cook evenly, and as they coagulate they are removed and placed to drain on a sieve or hair sieve.
When all the whites are cooked, remove the milk from the fire and incorporate four yolks, stirring the milk strongly and quickly, so that it gains consistency without curdling.
Place the eggs in a pyramid on a platter and pour the cream or milk over them, prepared as explained above.

As soon as the whites set, begin adding the yolks.
Sprinkle with salt, pepper, and dried parsley.

title: Huevos Fritos (Fried Eggs)
description: Prepared with eggs and pork or lard or oil.

ingredients.name: Pork lard or oil (ten times the volume of an egg for every half dozen eggs)
ingredients.sourceText: Pork lard or oil (ten times the volume of an egg for every half dozen eggs)

steps: Fry the eggs in pork lard or oil; the fat must be prepared so that the oil is free of bad smell and acrid flavor, and the lard is entirely anhydrous, without water
Make the fried eggs one at a time, and serve as they are made, immediately from the pan to the plate
In a large pan, add lard or oil in a quantity ten times greater than the volume of an egg, calculated for frying half a dozen
Break the egg, put the white in one cup and the yolk in another, agitate the white lightly without beating it
Put the pan over high heat
When the liquid is hot, it will smoke with a thin vapor that takes on a brownish color, turning into the characteristic blue smoke of all fats when boiling begins

At that moment, remove the pan from the fire, pour the white in a stream from about a hand's breadth of height, as if decanting, and immediately, without losing time and with great speed, throw the yolk in the middle

description: Prepared with eggs and lard or oil.
steps: When the lard or oil is ready for frying, add the egg that has been previously emptied into a cup.

With a dry skimmer, gradually fold up the white until you can flip the egg, which will look like a fritter if the operation is carried out quickly and over high heat.
Serve the eggs thus fried with puffed potatoes and shoestring potatoes, serving everything together in elegant disorder on a napkin, on a silver or Ruolz plate.

title: Huevos Hilados (Threaded Eggs)
description: Prepared with egg yolks, sugar, and water.
steps: Clarify {{source-0}} in {{source-1}}, taking care that the point is weak, as soon as it begins to thread.
Sift two dozen yolks through a clear sieve with the aid of a spatula, and add them gradually to the clarified sugar, stirring very quickly during cooking, which will last two minutes.

This mass or paste is poured into a funnel of cylindrical form, whose bottom is like that of a metal strainer, with holes the size the egg threads should have, and these are collected in very cold water, aiding their passage through the funnel with a wooden pestle or handle that weighs and presses the mass.

title: Huevos Pasados por Agua (Soft-Boiled Eggs)
description: Prepared with eggs and water.
steps: Place the eggs to be soft-boiled in cold water, covering them well

Serve the eggs to the table in a bowl or covered dish, filled with the water in which they cooked, cooled slightly with cold water to stop all cooking while preserving the heat
The eggs will be uniformly soft-boiled with slightly set yolks and milky, loose, and uniform whites
Use only very fresh eggs for this preparation

description: Prepared with eggs, beef, and breadcrumbs.
steps: Hard boil the eggs and cut them in half lengthwise or crosswise.

Serve separately with tomato sauce or béchamel sprinkled with pieces of fried ham.

title: Huevos á la Turca (Turkish Eggs)
description: Prepared with eggs, truffles, and beef.

ingredients.name: cooked, cold cow's milk
ingredients.sourceText: 2 tablespoons of cooked, cold cow's milk

steps: Brush the truffles clean and cut them into small pieces.
Sauté the truffles in a pan with beef butter over high heat.
Beat the egg whites until foamy in one bowl.
In 2 tablespoons of cooked, cold milk, beat the yolks, incorporating parsley, salt, pepper, clove, and nutmeg.
Combine the yolks with the whites and continue beating, then add half an ounce of beef butter in a piece.
Pour the mixture into the pan with the truffles.
Stir and turn the eggs with a wooden spatula until the mixture is uniform and gelatinous in consistency.
This operation takes only a few seconds.
Present with croutons fried in pork butter, cut into squares, rounds, or triangles.

title: Hígado de Cerdo a la Cazadora (Pork Liver Hunter's Style)
description: Prepared with pork liver, bacon, and shallots.
steps: Place in a serving dish with refined oil a pork liver, which is split lengthwise down the middle without the two pieces separating, so that it looks like an open lamb kidney.
Then make incisions lengthwise and crosswise, as if it were gridded like a bar of chocolate, and the grooves or marks of the cuts are filled with a hash of bacon, parsley and shallots minced.
After two hours, moisten the entire surface of the liver with the oil that is in the dish, and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Then close the liver, which was open like a book, lard it with thin leaves of bacon and roast it in the oven or on the plate, in a roasting pan or baking sheet.
When the liver is well cooked, place it on the serving platter, skim the fat from the roasting juice and strain it to pour over the dish, strengthened with lemon juice.

ingredients.name: rum or cognac

steps: Trim the pork liver into small equal pieces and sauté in a pan with beef butter, turning frequently so that the cooking is uniform.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper, and remove the liver pieces from the pan when they are slightly overcooked.
In the fat from the sauté, add finely chopped fine herbs and shallots and half a tablespoon of flour, with one ladle of broth and a thin stream of vinegar.
Once the sauce is bound, return the liver pieces to the pan so that they are soaked and cooked in the sauce, just for two minutes, adding {{source-9}} to aromatize the dish at the moment of serving.

title: Hígado de Raya (Skate Liver)
description: Prepared with liver, bread, and onions.
steps: Cut slices of bread that are twice as long as they are wide and soak them in raw oil
Fry the bread slices in cow's milk butter to make canapés
Melt 125 grams of cow's milk butter in a pot and stew and cook the skate livers in it with plenty of chopped parsley, small onions, shallots, and capers, all chopped very finely
When the liver is cooked, remove it from the pot and set aside
Place the fried bread slices on an oval metal platter
Spread each piece of bread first with a layer of the finely chopped vegetables cooked in their liquid
Place a piece of skate liver on top of each bread slice with a couple of anchovy fillets, then finish with a second spreading of the fine herbs mixture
Once all the canapés are garnished equally, sprinkle them with very finely crumbled soft bread
Cover the platter with a bell cover loaded with a small amount of coals just to brown the surface of the dish

title: Jamón en Dulce (Glazed Ham)
description: Prepared with ham, white wine, and water.

ingredients.name: three bottles of superior white wine (preferably Sherry)
ingredients.sourceText: three bottles of superior white wine (preferably Sherry)

steps: Cook the ham in water over low heat for twelve hours in a quantity such that the water is consumed at the end of that time.
Debone the ham, trim and arrange it in the shape of a loaf or cake, and wrap and sew it very tightly in a piece of linen cloth, well washed and rewashed.

Cook for twenty-four hours over low heat and until the liquid is consumed, in three bottles of superior white wine—Sherry preferably—taking care that the pot or pan is deep so that the wine bathes the ham well.
Add a little thyme, rosemary, spearmint, nutmeg and a few leaves of tarragon.
Cover the pot well so that all the steam from the boiling is consumed inside.
After twenty-four hours, remove the ham and place it, without removing the wrapping, in a dish or mold of proportionate size.
Place much weight on top with small boards to press it well.
When it is completely cold, overturn the mold and place and unwrap the ham on a platter, arranging it for presentation according to the aesthetic preferences of the preparer.
If you want it to make a good appearance, dust its surface with sugar, which is burned or browned with a hot iron.

Allow it to cool and serve with the aspic that has formed

title: Jugo de Carne (Meat Juice)
description: Prepared with beef, veal, and carrot.

ingredients.name: Parsley, chervil, tarragon, bay leaf, and thyme in proper proportion
ingredients.sourceText: Parsley, chervil, tarragon, bay leaf, and thyme in proper proportion

steps: Cut the beef rump and veal rump into pieces the size of plums.
Place them in a saucepan with a large carrot and a large onion, cut into thin slices.
Make a small bundle with parsley, chervil, tarragon, bay leaf, and thyme, tied with white thread, and add this seasoning.
Season with clove, nutmeg, salt, and a pinch of pepper if desired.
Note that the seasoning should err on the side of being bland, as any strong spice would be inconvenient for sauces in which the juice will be used.
Cover the saucepan and sweat over high heat, moving the utensil frequently.

When the pieces of meat and the pieces of onion and carrot begin to brown, and when the juice they release sticks to the saucepan, add cold water in sufficient quantity so that everything is completely covered, without excess water.
Without stopping stirring with a spatula, scrape up the juice that is stuck to the saucepan.
Add the veal foot or hand, cut into three or four pieces.

title: Langosta a la Americana (Lobster American Style)
description: Prepared with lobster, onions, and white wine.

ingredients.name: four large onions the size of eggs
ingredients.sourceText: four large onions the size of eggs

steps: Cook the lobster in the natural way, that is, in cold water in which it bathes well, remove it at the first boil and let it cool to completely remove the shell.
Cut the tail into large pieces and place them in a deep serving dish that can go to the fire forming a ring.
With the meat from the legs and everything found in the interior of the head make a very fine chopped mixture, and with it fill the hollow of the ring.

Sauté well in a saucepan with butter from Isigny four large onions the size of eggs, chop them very finely, and after three minutes, the sautéed mixture, moisten with dry white wine and let cook half an hour.
Then add Spanish sauce and tomato puree in equal parts, and a hint of Cayenne pepper.
Reduce the sauce by two-thirds over vivid fire, and strain through fine sieve, pouring it into the serving dish over the lobster.
Ten minutes before serving this dish, prepared as has been said, cook in the oven, over gentle fire for a quarter of an hour.

steps: Embed symmetrically in the meaty part of the leg of mutton twelve garlic cloves and twice as many fillets of well-washed anchovies, as if they were larding strips of bacon
Roast the meat in the same manner and with the care recommended for roasted leg of mutton
While the meat is roasting, peel one liter of garlic cloves
Blanch the garlic by scalding it in boiling water, submerging it repeatedly in different waters, then let it cool in fresh water
Cook the garlic in a bowl of broth
When the leg of mutton is roasted to its point, well degrease the juice it has released
Serve the meat with the garnish of garlic

title: Leg of Mutton Scottish Style (Pierna de Carnero á la Escocesa)
description: Prepared with leg of mutton, bay leaf, and chervil.
steps: In a large pot where the leg can fit comfortably, boil a large quantity of water with pepper, salt, thyme, bay leaf, all manner of spices, parsley, chervil, onions and carrots.
When the water boils vigorously, place the leg in the pot, cover tightly and continue cooking vigorously without stopping for an instant.
Cook for as many quarter hours as the leg weighs in pounds. For example, if it weighs four pounds, cook for one hour.
Remove immediately from the pot and serve with white sauce and trimmed pickled cucumbers.

title: Leg of Mutton Stewed Manchegan Style (Pierna de Carnero Estofada á la Manchega)
description: Prepared with leg of mutton, bacon, and red wine.
steps: Bone the leg of mutton well and lard it with aged bacon, seasoning with some excess of spices.
Place in a pot where the meat fits comfortably.
Cook in a quarter liter of red wine and two spoonfuls of vinegar, with six onions the size of a hen's egg, turnips, carrots, aromatic herbs, a couple of garlic cloves and a hint of pepper.
Cook this very slowly for four hours with the pot well covered.
Serve with a little of its degreased broth.

title: Leg of Mutton with Other Legumes (Pierna de Carnero con Otras Legumbres)
description: Prepared with leg of mutton.
steps: Prepare the leg as previously described.
Cook the legumes beforehand in water and have them ready.
Half an hour before serving, incorporate the well-drained legumes into the meat and its juices after vaporizing the water they contain.
Allow them to stew slowly, cooking gently for about fifteen minutes, during which time they will absorb the meat juices.
Instead of beans, by the same procedure, the leg can be served with cauliflower, pea purée, sorrel paste or spinach paste, lentils, etc.

title: Leg of Mutton with Testicles (Pierna de Carnero con Criadillas)
description: Prepared with leg of mutton, mutton, and bacon.
steps: After removing the bone from the leg of mutton and taking out half a pound of meat from the center, mince it with testicles to replace the removed part.
Lard with thick bacon and tie.
Lard again with testicles cut into thin strips.
Keep this way for twenty-four hours.
After that time, cook over low fire, surrounded by strips of bacon and moistened with white wine.
Strain the sauce, reduce it and serve.

title: Lengua de Vaca a la Escarlata (Beef Tongue Scarlet Style)
description: Prepared with beef tongue, saltpeter, and sausage.
steps: Remove the hard, rough part of the tongue by holding it over live coals until the skin loosens.
After separating the skin, rub the tongue with pepper and saltpeter.
In a terrine, on a layer of salt, place the tongue and cover it completely with more salt mixed with cloves, thyme, and laurel.
After 24 hours, add more salt, and do so every day so the tongue is continuously bathed in this brine.
After fifteen days, remove the tongue from its marinade, drain it very well, and introduce it into a casing as if it were sausage.
Tie the two ends of the casing very well so it fits snugly, and hang it in the smoke for several days in a fireplace where wood is burning, but high enough so it does not become charred.
When ready to cook the tongue, soak it first for five hours.
Then place it in a pot full of water with thyme, laurel, and cloves. Cook for six hours over very low heat.
Let it cool in its own broth, and remove it clean of adhering fat.
Serve cold as a cold dish, either sliced on plates as you would serve sausage, or alternating slices with ham in aspic or turkey galantine, as a cold appetizer at a luncheon or light meal.

title: Lengua de Vaca en Pepitoria (Beef Tongue in Pepitoria Sauce)
description: A sauce made with beef tongue, beef broth, and white wine.
steps: Cut the cooked tongue into strips after peeling it.
Simmer very gently in a saucepan with one cup of broth and one quarter liter of white wine.
Season moderately with salt and pepper.
When the broth has reduced by half, arrange the slices symmetrically on a serving dish.
Away from heat, incorporate into the sauce finely chopped parsley and two egg yolks diluted in a little broth with a dash of vinegar.
Pour the thickened sauce over the tongue at the moment of serving.

title: Lengua de Vaca en Salsa Picante (Beef Tongue in Spicy Sauce)
description: A sauce made with beef tongue, carrots, and onions.
steps: Cook the tongue as you would meat for a stew, with carrots, onions, and a celery stalk.
Six hours of cooking is better than five.

title: Lenguado al Gratín (Sole Gratinée)
description: Prepared with sole, white wine, and sauce.
steps: Choose fish for four persons; remove the gills, intestines and black skin; scale the white skin, wash and dry.
Make an incision on the skinless side of half a centimeter deep on each side of the spine, without touching it, tilting the knife from left to right.
Clean, then place in an oval dish thirty grams of butter, two deciliters of white wine, two pinches of salt, and two pinches of pepper.
Place the sole also and let it cook for five minutes, covering it with two spoonfuls of Italian sauce and sprinkling with a layer of grated and toasted breadcrumbs of half a centimeter.
Cover the gratin dish with the baking dish cover, with moderate fire on top, as there will also be on the stove, ensuring that cooking is not interrupted.
Serve at quarter of an hour.

title: Lenguados al Estilo de Normandía (Sole in the Style of Normandy)
description: Prepared with sole, onion, and white wine.
steps: After cleaning the fish, remove the skin if very large and place on butter in a fish kettle or baking dish where it fits comfortably.

Add parsley, thyme, chopped onion, a glass of good white wine and another of broth or water, salt, pepper powder, grated nutmeg, twelve oysters and twelve clams which have been briefly boiled to remove them from their shells and make them white, and some truffle pieces or earthnut truffles, putting it all on the fire with a little butter.
For the oysters and clams sauce: in another pan or small saucepan, fry lightly small strips of veal and ham or bacon without browning them.
Add half a spoonful of flour, stir everything very well and add a little broth, a small onion, carrot slices, pepper, nutmeg, bay leaves, and some salt.
When the meat is cooked, add this strained broth and sauce over the sole.
Place on the fire to cook, covering it with fire also on the baking dish cover.
After the fish is cooked, place it on the plate and add some mushrooms cooked with lemon juice, small slices of bread moistened with milk and fried in butter to serve it very hot.

title: Liebre Asada (Roasted Hare)
description: Prepared with hare, bacon, and lard.

ingredients.name: Cow or pig lard for sautéing
ingredients.sourceText: Cow or pig lard for sautéing

steps: A hare can be roasted without larding, but it tastes better when the meatier parts are larded with very fine strips of bacon

Since hare meat does not have enough consistency to lard raw, once the hare is ready and prepared to go into the roaster, sauté it in cow or pig lard in a pan and only briefly, just enough for the meat to firm up slightly and acquire tenderness

title: Liebre Guisada (Stewed Hare)
description: Prepared with hare, white wine, and butter or bacon.
steps: Cut the hare into pieces and soak in white wine.

Cook for at least two hours.

title: Macarones Verdes (Pappardelle) (Green Pappardelle)
description: Prepared with spinach, beef fat, and broth.
steps: Cook a bunch of spinach with water and salt, and once fully cooked, pound it.
Mix this paste with a dough composed of four eggs, half a pound of flour, and two ounces of beef fat.
Mix everything well with a rolling pin, extending it on a board.
Cut into strips similar to noodles, leaving them to dry in the sun. This appears to be indispensable, as oven heat is not suitable.
Once well dried, cook them in meat broth.
Serve sprinkled with Parmesan cheese.

title: Macaroni al Gratín (Macaroni Gratin)
description: Prepared with macaroni, parmesan cheese, and breadcrumbs.
steps: Cook the macaroni as in previous recipes.
Line a small gratin dish with a thin layer of butter.
Fill it with the macaroni, forming a mound approximately six centimeters high.
Sprinkle with 30 grams of grated Parmesan cheese and half a tablespoon of toasted breadcrumbs.
Melt 15 grams of butter and pour it over the macaroni.
Place over low heat and cover with an iron lid with quite hot coals on top.
If the burner flame is lit properly, the macaroni should be cooked in ten minutes.
For fast days, macaroni gratin can also be made by substituting the broth with milk.

title: Macaroni al Jugo (Macaroni with Meat Gravy)
description: A sauce made with macaroni, parmesan cheese, and beef fat or pork fat.

ingredients.name: beef fat or pork fat
ingredients.sourceText: 2 ounces beef fat or pork fat

ingredients.name: 1 large onion the size of a fist
ingredients.sourceText: 1 large onion the size of a fist

steps: Cook the macaroni in plenty of water over high heat, seasoning with salt.
After a few minutes of cooking, and taking care that they do not fall apart and remain somewhat firm, remove and drain.
Arrange the macaroni in a deep dish in layers interspersed with finely grated Parmesan cheese.
Pour the meat gravy over everything at the moment of serving.
To prepare the gravy for two pounds of macaroni: brown two pounds of sirloin in a saucepan with two ounces of beef fat or pork fat.
Add one large onion the size of a fist, parsley, two ounces of bacon, and spices, chopping everything very fine.
When the onion is consumed without darkening, moisten with one glass of water and increase the fire, then add three pounds of well-cleaned and crumbled tomatoes.
As the tomato quickly reduces, add the water calculated for the desired quantity of gravy and leave everything to cook over low heat for two hours.
Remove the meat, which can be eaten cold at another meal, and pour the broth or gravy over the macaroni.

Half-cook two pounds of macaroni by dropping them into a large quantity of boiling water, seasoning with salt.
Remove from the pot or saucepan and place in a colander to drain the water.
In a very clarified oil and in a skillet, fry two pounds of tomatoes; season and pass through a fine sieve to obtain a thick broth.
Place the macaroni in a deep, round serving dish.
Pour the tomato sauce over and cover the entire surface with halves of raw tomatoes, upon which drop some raw oil.
Place the dish in the oven under high heat for fifteen minutes and serve.

title: Magdalena Picón (Picón's Madeleine Cake)
description: A cake made with butter, sugar, and flour.

ingredients.name: butter for melting
ingredients.sourceText: two ounces of butter for melting

ingredients.name: a quarter pound of ground sugar
ingredients.sourceText: a quarter pound of ground sugar

ingredients.name: lemon zest equal to about one teaspoon of coffee
ingredients.sourceText: lemon zest equal to about one teaspoon of coffee

steps: Melt two ounces of butter in a pan
Grease a mold or cake pan with melted butter on the inside and let it cool
In the pan, add a quarter pound of ground sugar and another quarter pound of flour, with lemon zest equal to about one teaspoon of coffee
Beat and mix all this with the melted butter until forming a homogeneous and crumbly mixture, like sand
Add two eggs, whites and yolks
Stir and beat with a spatula to bind the batter, like thick pap
Fill the greased mold and bake this in twenty minutes at a strong oven heat
Let cool and remove from the mold

title: Manjar Blanco (Almond Blanc Mange)
description: Prepared with almond, sweet almonds, and jelly.

ingredients.name: twenty bitter almond kernels, all peeled
ingredients.sourceText: twenty bitter almond kernels, all peeled

ingredients.name: three glasses of simple jelly, somewhat warmed
ingredients.sourceText: three glasses of simple jelly, somewhat warmed

steps: Prepare by putting {{source-0}} and twenty bitter almond kernels in cold water infusion for twenty-four hours, all of them peeled.

Pound them immediately, sprinkling during this operation with some spoonfuls of very cold water; and when no fragment is distinguishable from them and the paste has enough homogeneity, add four or five glasses of water, strain this mass first through a cloth, pressing it with force, and then through a napkin.
Mix three glasses of simple jelly, somewhat more than lukewarm, and empty the resulting liquid into the mold.

title: Manos de Ternera en Salsa (Veal Hands in Sauce)
description: A sauce made with veal, onion, and hazelnuts.
steps: Soak the hands in very hot water for a considerable time.
Clean and peel carefully to remove all skin residue.
Cook at low heat for five hours.
Transfer to another pot with the prepared sauce.
The sauce should contain: onion, parsley, finely ground roasted hazelnuts, a little nutmeg, a pinch of pepper, and two bay leaves.
Cook the hands in this sauce for another hour at low heat.
A few minutes before removing from heat, sprinkle with several spoonfuls of white wine from Rueda.
Serve hot.

title: Manos de Ternera Rellenas (Stuffed Veal Hands)
description: Prepared with veal, sauce, and wine.
steps: Carefully debone the veal hands, splitting them only along the inside edge without damaging them.
Cook the hands in their natural state, then drain and let cool.
Fill the hollow with a well-seasoned quenelle stuffing.
Tie with twine to prevent the filling from escaping.
Cook for another half hour in Spanish sauce with one glass of Jerez wine.
Remove the twine as you place each hand on the serving platter.
Pour the cooking sauce over top and serve.

title: Mantequilla de Cangrejos (Crab Butter)
description: Prepared with crabs and beef.
steps: Dry the crabs in the oven
Pound them in a mortar until they are converted to powder
Knead the powder with the beef lard and place everything over low heat so that the lard liquefies
Pass and squeeze by compression through a metal sieve placed over a vessel filled with cold water
As the crab butter passes through the strainer and falls into the water, it will solidify
Remove the solidified butter from the water and shape it, while cleaning and drying it with a white cloth, repeating as many times as necessary to remove all moisture

Add some water and two egg whites beaten until they reach the consistency of snow with powdered sugar and a pinch of sifted gum arabic
Mix everything together
Knead for half an hour

description: Prepared with butter and water.

ingredients.name: cow butter per pound of flour
ingredients.sourceText: One pound of cow butter per pound of flour

Brush the surface well with cow butter
Fold in half
Pass the rolling pin over it again and brush again with butter and flour
Repeat this process as many times as desired to create layers, at least three times

title: Masa para Bollos (Dough for Rolls)
description: A bread preparation made with beer or yeast or flour or dough, flour, and water.

ingredients.name: Beer yeast, one ounce per pound of flour amasada, or one ounce per four pounds of dough
ingredients.sourceText: Beer yeast, one ounce per pound of flour amasada, or one ounce per four pounds of dough

ingredients.name: Cow butter, one good quarter-pound per pound of flour
ingredients.sourceText: Cow butter, one good quarter-pound per pound of flour

ingredients.name: Three eggs per pound of flour
ingredients.sourceText: Three eggs per pound of flour

ingredients.name: Fine salt, two grams per pound of flour
ingredients.sourceText: Fine salt, two grams per pound of flour

steps: Begin by making a leaven: place a mound of flour on the table, about one quarter of the total flour to be used
Make a hole in the middle and add beer yeast
Pour lukewarm water over it and knead well
Place the dough in a trough, make two cuts in the shape of a cross, cover with a cloth and let it ferment
When the leaven has acquired the required quality, knead separately the rest of the flour with cow butter, eggs and fine salt
Join the leaven to the dough and fold the dough many times, sprinkling it with flour
Let it rest at least eight hours before making the rolls

title: Merluza a la Inglesa (Hake in the English Style)
description: Prepared with hake, lemon juice, and egg yolks.
steps: Take a large piece of hake and after cleaning and removing the central bone, split in two from top to bottom
Clean both pieces well of small bones and skin, leaving only the two rounded loins
Cut into thin slices across, about half a finger thick, and flatten them carefully
Season with salt and lemon juice, place on a strainer to drain for a time. Dry with a cloth
Pass through melted cow butter mixed with egg yolks, then coat with breadcrumbs, pressing with the knife blade
Place the well-prepared pieces in a pot or pan with melted cow butter. With all remaining meat, make a forcemeat to fill a smooth mold, which will be cooked in a water bath one hour before

At serving time, reheat the pieces, being careful they brown on both sides. Empty the mold onto the platter, placing on top cooked potatoes mashed into the shape of purée and around the pieces alternated with slices of fried bread, and separately a butter sauce if desired

title: Merluza a lo Imprevisto (Hake Prepared Unexpectedly)
description: Prepared with hake, shallots, and chervil.

ingredients.name: the best butter, from Isigny or Montpellier
ingredients.sourceText: Two ounces of the best butter, from Isigny or Montpellier

steps: Cook the whole hake in water without any seasoning, in a short broth; leave in the fish kettle away from the fire to serve in a platter, after the fish is drained, with its sauce on top
For the sauce: reheat two ounces of the best butter in it, sweating shallots, parsley, chervil, and one clove of garlic, all very finely chopped
Add one spoonful of flour toasted to medium color and some water to dilute it
Cut small pickles like capers and, as the French say, blanch them, then bind the sauce with an egg yolk dissolved in cold water

title: Merluza Asada (Roasted Hake)
description: Prepared with hake, beef, and white wine.

ingredients.name: hake pieces from the middle body downward, including the tail
ingredients.sourceText: hake pieces from the middle body downward, including the tail

ingredients.name: white wine, about half a quarter-liter for a quarter-pound of butter and three pounds of hake
ingredients.sourceText: white wine, about half a quarter-liter for a quarter-pound of butter and three pounds of hake

steps: Take the piece or pieces of hake desired from the middle body downward, including the tail.
Soak the pieces and remove the scales, then dry them with a napkin.
Place them on wire grills to roast over low heat until they are golden on all sides.
Melt beef butter in a pan and remove the foam it releases.
Add about half a quarter-liter of white wine for the quantity of a quarter-pound of butter and three pounds of hake with breadcrumbs and chopped parsley.
Let the sauce boil only once, pouring it over the pieces and serving them promptly.
Proportion the quantity of white wine proportionally according to the amount of butter and hake used.

title: Migas al Estilo de Teruel (Crumbs in the Style of Teruel)
description: Prepared with bread, garlic, and water.

ingredients.name: Bread two or three days old
ingredients.sourceText: Bread two or three days old

steps: Take bread that is two or three days old and divide it in half.
Taking either half, make vertical cuts at its angles, and then horizontal cuts, so that small pieces the size of chickpeas result. The crust is better than the crumb.
After cutting, place them in a napkin and pour a little water over them, stirring well so they become evenly moistened.
Dust them with salt, as fine as possible, in the necessary quantity.
This must be done at night, and wrapped in the same napkin so it does not lose moisture, keep them until the following day.
Half an hour before the time set for breakfast, fry oil in a pan, burning two garlic cloves.
When the oil is at its point, remove the garlic and add the crumbs all at once, stirring constantly with a rasera or iron skimmer for twelve or fifteen minutes, and very hot, serve them to the table.

title: Migas Canas (Shepherd's Breadcrumbs with Milk)
description: Prepared with milk, kidneys, and bread.

ingredients.name: half the kidneys of a ewe
ingredients.sourceText: half the kidneys of a ewe

steps: Place an iron cauldron over the fire.
Add a good piece of tallow to the cauldron, along with half the kidneys of a ewe.
While the tallow melts, take a wooden plate that is quite deep and crumble two bread rolls in it as if for soup.

Once the tallow is melted and the solid residues have been removed, add one piece of bread to the cauldron and let it brown there for at least two minutes to remove the raw taste from the tallow, then remove it and discard.
Add the bread prepared in the wooden plate, crumbled as for soup, and press it slightly with a wooden spoon.
Using the wooden spoon held upside down (with the back facing up), pour about half a quart of water over it so it falls scattered, moistening all the bread.
Add a bit of well-ground salt immediately.

As soon as the cauldron begins to steam, start stirring and crumbling the bread with the spoon, and from time to time take the cauldron by its handle and give it a special shake (a mixture of force and skill), turning over the entire mass so what is below comes to the top and vice versa.
After ten more minutes, remove the cauldron from the fire.
Make a hole in the middle of the breadcrumbs with the spoon and pour in freshly milked goat's milk, which transforms the dish into migas canas (breadcrumbs with milk).

title: Migas de Ministro (Minister's Breadcrumbs)
description: Prepared with rolls, garlic, and bacon.

ingredients.name: one quarter pound of bacon, cut into pieces
ingredients.sourceText: one quarter pound of bacon, cut into pieces

steps: Cut two French rolls into walnut-sized pieces and place them in a bowl or mortar with salt, sweet paprika, two finely chopped garlic cloves, and watered milk so the bread becomes well moistened without becoming too soggy.
Invert one bowl over another (the second without an opening) and, holding both with your hands, shake them vigorously by inclining the first bowl's opening downward so any excess water can drain out.
When done, the salt and paprika will be well mixed with the bread.
In a frying pan over high heat, add one quarter pound of bacon pieces, and when it has released half of its fat, pour it over the bread.
Cover again with one bowl over another and shake them anew, while the remaining bacon in the pan melts and becomes golden brown.
Then add the bread to the pan, and without setting down the skimmer, crush and pound it while it fries and absorbs all the fat.

When the breadcrumbs are dry on the outside and saturated with fat on the inside, and when the pan is clean and shining without a drop of oil, remove them and arrange them in a dome shape on a napkin placed on a serving platter.

title: Migas Vanguardia (Avant-Garde Crumbs)
description: Prepared with bread, garlic, and water.

ingredients.name: Oil in quantity equal to the volume of bread
ingredients.sourceText: Oil in quantity equal to the volume of bread

ingredients.name: Half a dozen garlic heads, whole and separated into cloves
ingredients.sourceText: Half a dozen garlic heads, whole and separated into cloves

steps: Cut slices from the loaf one finger thick and soak them in water seasoned with salt to taste.
Drain the water and dry the bread slices with a napkin.
Heat oil in a pan or skillet in quantity equal to the volume of bread.
When the oil is very hot, fry and burn half a dozen garlic heads, whole and with their cloves separated.
Remove and discard the garlic, and over high heat fry the bread slices in that oil until their surfaces are toasted.
Then, holding the pan firmly with one hand, crumble the bread with the other, armed with a spatula or skimmer, crumbling everything equally, without interrupting the frying.

Once all the bread pieces are well colored and have acquired a certain hardness and looseness, remove the crumbs and serve them, dusting with a little salt or with sugar, according to whether they are to be eaten with another dish or alone.

title: Mondongo Veracruzano (Veracruz-Style Tripe Stew)
description: Prepared with lemon juice, corn, and veal or pork.
steps: Clean the mondongo with hot water and lemon juice, cut into small pieces, and place in a casserole with water, salt, and dried corn.
Add a veal or pork foot for substance and flavor, and bring to a boil.
When the meat is tender, add finely chopped pumpkin, yuca, malanga, sweet potato, and plantains cut in half.
When everything is well cooked, add saffron threads, raisins, toasted almonds, two spoonfuls of capers with their vinegar, and herbs.
Let cook for about an hour, remove from heat, let rest a bit, and serve hot.

title: Otras Salsas Españolas (Other Spanish Sauces)
description: A sauce made with broth, game, and white wine.
steps: Boil and skim the foam in a casserole a certain quantity of broth, to which the substance of small game and poultry will be added, and if desired juice, defatting it and straining through a sieve.

Also prepare with equal parts of substance and broth, a glass of white wine, a bundle of parsley, a small onion, a bay leaf, a head of garlic, two cloves, two or three spoonfuls of oil, a bundle of cilantro, an onion sliced in rings, all of which should boil for two hours, then defatted and salt and pepper added.
With testicles, mushrooms and sufficient quantity of substance or defatted broth, the same sauce as before is achieved.

The meatless sauce is made by lining the bottom of a casserole with oil, and placing in it carrots, onions cut in rings, and slices of fish of all kinds; immediately moisten with meatless broth and bring to boil. Add garlic, mushrooms and white wine until everything reduces to a regular consistency.
