title: Pasta de Espinacas (Spinach Paste)
description: Prepared with beef or pork or butter, egg yolk, and water.

ingredients.name: One quarter pound of beef or pork butter
ingredients.sourceText: One quarter pound of beef or pork butter

steps: Wash the spinaches and cut them in any manner.
According to the volume they make, place on high heat a pot with water in quantity four or six times greater than that of the vegetable.

When it boils in bubbles, add the spinaches and coarse salt by handfuls—that is, a great deal of salt. After ten minutes of violent boiling of the water, and without covering the vessel, remove the spinaches and submerge them in a basin or bucket of cold water.

Remove them from there immediately and place in fresh cold water, leaving them for five minutes, after which add them one last time in another cold water, where they can remain ten minutes, or as long as an hour, until beginning to season them.
Remove the spinaches from the water, drain and discharge all the water they contain, and set aside on a platter.

In a pan or baking dish, melt afterwards one quarter pound of beef or pork butter, and before it is very russet add a couple of tablespoons of flour, and without letting it take color moisten it all to form a somewhat clear pap with the water in which the vegetables cooked; season well, let cook a couple of minutes and remove from the heat.

Once the spinaches are dry, chop them very finely on a board, and with their own water, in small quantities, pass the resolved paste through a fine sieve, collecting it in the vessel in which the pap is prepared.
Mix and blend well; give it a boil so that all that mass comes together, and away from the heat bind it with an egg yolk, dissolved in two tablespoons of water.
To serve this dish place it on a round platter, in a heap or spherical casque, studding its surface with croutons and hard boiled eggs split in half and symmetrically presented.

title: Pasta Española (Spanish Batter for Frying)
description: Prepared with cognac or rum, milk or water, and flour.

ingredients.name: milk diluted in water or water
ingredients.sourceText: milk diluted in water or water

steps: Place the flour on a plate and make a hollow in the middle. For half a pound of flour, add one egg, salt, and pepper to taste, and one spoonful of aguardiente, cognac, or rum. Mix everything very well together.
Add milk diluted in water or water alone gradually until the batter has only the consistency necessary to coat the dishes with a layer the thickness of a small dog's paw.
Mix well and beat with a metal fork, then let it rest for one hour.
At the moment of using this batter, add half of an egg white beaten until stiff peaks form, but only if you want the fried dish to puff up considerably.
Note that this puffing has the disadvantage of impregnating the dish heavily with grease.
This batter can also be used to fry fish, but as a general rule and for better taste, fried fish comes out better with simple flouring.

title: Pasta Francesa (French Batter for Frying)
description: Prepared with flour, water, and butter.

ingredients.name: one quarter liter of warm water
ingredients.sourceText: one quarter liter of warm water

steps: Place 250 grams of flour in a deep plate and gradually add one quarter liter of warm water, enough so that sixty grams of very fresh butter soften and melt.
The key to this batter is in how you work it so that it is uniformly bound together and has a consistency like that of well-made chocolate.
If not all of the warm water is necessary to reach this state, part of the butter may remain on the surface of the unused water, and in this case it should be collected with a spoon.

title: Pastel Caliente de Codornices (Hot Quail Pastry)
description: A pastry dish made with pastry, quails, and clarified butter.

ingredients.name: Three hundred grams of calf liver
ingredients.sourceText: Three hundred grams of calf liver

ingredients.name: Two hundred fifty grams of bacon
ingredients.sourceText: Two hundred fifty grams of bacon

steps: Make a pastry mold as described in the previous article
Prepare eight quails by cutting them lengthwise in two parts
Place them in a sauté pan with clarified butter
Season with salt and pepper and sauté over the fire for ten minutes
Drain and let cool
Make a filling by placing diced bacon in a sauté pan and adding salt and pepper
Sauté for four minutes, then add the calf liver also cut into small dice
Sauté for another four minutes, let cool, mash everything and strain through a horsehair sieve
Put a ring of filling at the bottom of the pastry mold, two centimeters thick, leaving the rest of the mold uncovered
Place eight selected half quails all turned the same side in the pastry mold, putting a bed of filling between them to hold them up
Form a second layer of filling and quails in the same manner
In the hollow left in the center of the rings, place a bread plug wrapped in a slice of bacon
Put a layer of filling over the quails and cover with the pastry lid, fluted and glazed, and bake in the oven
When the pastry is cooked, remove the lid and the bread plug from the center
Place the pastry on the serving dish and pour crumbled truffles inside
On top arrange a garnish of chicken sweetbreads and cover with crumbled truffles that project above the sweetbreads

title: Pastel Caliente à la Financiera (Hot Pastry à la Financière)
description: A pastry dish made with dough, sauce, and crayfish.
steps: Make a mold of empanada dough
Fill it with flour, cover it and flute the edge
When the dough is cooked, remove the lid, leaving a two-centimeter border
Remove the flour from the interior, brush the inside and outside with a pastry brush and dry in the oven for four minutes
Prepare a financière sauce
Make the garnish with five rooster crests, five crayfish, five mushrooms and a beautiful truffle
Fill the pastry with the sauce and arrange the garnish in pyramid form
Glaze the dough with clear glaze and serve

title: Pastel de Liebre (Hare Pastry)
description: A pastry dish made with hare, ham, and pork.
steps: Completely debone the hare and set aside the loins, cut each into three or four pieces, and the meat from the legs
Make a minced mixture with everything else, meat fibers, liver, etc.
Prepare an earthenware or porcelain pot that resists fire
Line the interior, bottom and walls, with thin bacon leaves
Place half of the minced mixture in the pot, and on top place the reserved pieces of deboned hare
Cover these pieces with the other half of the minced mixture, to which you can add thin slices of truffles or mushrooms
Moisten everything with one good glass of cognac
Close with bacon leaves as on the inside, ensuring the pot is completely full
Cover the pot with its lid and seal it with luten, a type of paste used to hermetically close vessels
Place in the oven at medium-strong heat and leave to cook for four hours
Allow to cool and serve in the pot at family tables

When wanting to give more solemnity to the dish, submerge the already-cold pot for two minutes in boiling water, and the hare pastry will detach easily, then place it on a platter by inverting the pot over it

title: Pastel de Perdices (Partridge Pie)
description: A pastry dish made with partridges, calf liver, and bacon.

ingredients.name: one hundred grams of fine fresh butter
ingredients.sourceText: one hundred grams of fine fresh butter

ingredients.name: one glass of Jerez or good common white wine
ingredients.sourceText: one glass of Jerez or good common white wine

steps: Cook the six partridges in water with the calf liver, fresh bacon, onions, turnips, and carrots with appropriate seasoning, spices, and aromatic herbs, for four hours in continuous, slow cooking.
Remove the partridges and debone them entirely.

With the remaining cooked ingredients except the aromatic herbs, make a picadillo that is converted into a paste by passing it through a food mill with the aid of the cooking broth, which should be reduced by half and thickened considerably.
In a pot, place one hundred grams of fine fresh butter and incorporate {{source-10}} to brown it lightly without toasting.
Moisten with one glass of Jerez or good common white wine.
Incorporate and mix the purée very well, ensuring it is somewhat loose, which is achieved with the auxiliary broth.
Fill an earthenware terrine of the kind used for pastels of this class.
Cook for one hour in a water bath.
When cold, this pastel can include truffle slices if desired, and when kept in a cool place it keeps perfectly for days.

title: Patatas Cocidas (Steamed Potatoes)
description: Prepared with potatoes, water, and salt.
steps: Place an iron pot on the heat with just enough water to moisten the bottom
Place two or three rounded stones the size of eggs in the pot
Fill the vessel with unpeeled potatoes so that water does not touch them
Fill the space above the potatoes with a strong cloth dampened in water and wrung out, as if it were a plug
Cover the pot with its lid and place a weight on top
Maintain a medium fire to keep water boiling; potatoes will cook in half an hour from the steam
Serve the potatoes in the basket or between the folds of a napkin in an elegant metal basket

steps: Put much oil in a pan and at the same time add potatoes cut into wheels.

title: Patatas Fritas (Fried Potatoes)
description: Prepared with potatoes and oil or lard.
steps: Use a quantity of fat four to ten times the volume of all the potatoes
Maintain a lively and consistent fire throughout the cooking time
Use a splendidly wide and deep pan in relation to the quantities of fat
Cut peeled potatoes into thin wheels the size of a coin, into small squares the length of a paper cigar and one centimeter thick, or into thin sticks using a cutting apparatus

For thin sticks: hold one handle of the cutting device with the left hand and place the other handle into one of the handles of a bowl positioned on the work table; with the same left hand grasp the other handle of the bowl; with the right hand cut the potatoes by passing them over the cuts of the device, pressing firmly and in one direction
When cut into sticks, place immediately into very hot oil and remove at once

For wheels or small squares, keep them cut in a bowl of water; when ready to fry, remove with hand, place in a strainer, turn them over to drain a little, and while still wet, place in the hot oil where they will sizzle but fry better

title: Pato Asado (Roasted Duck)
description: Prepared with duck and butter or lard.
steps: Spit the duck on a roasting spit after cleaning and preparing it.
Remove excess fat beforehand.
Roast slowly over the fire so that the remaining fat melts gently.
When cooking is nearly complete, increase the heat so the duck takes on color.
Serve on a layer of croutons soaked in its fat, with the roasting juice in a gravy boat, completely free of grease.

title: Pato con Nabos ó con Aceitunas (Duck with Turnips or with Olives)
description: Prepared with duck, olives, and bacon.

ingredients.name: Bacon leaves, larger than the duck and one finger thick
ingredients.sourceText: Bacon leaves, larger than the duck and one finger thick

ingredients.name: Two slices of very lean veal
ingredients.sourceText: Two slices of very lean veal

ingredients.name: Turnips cut into small chunks, or parsnips
ingredients.sourceText: Turnips cut into small chunks, or parsnips

steps: Clean and prepare the duck, and tie its wings with twine.
Place the duck in a pot between two leaves of bacon.
Add two slices of very lean veal, two carrots, two onions with their cloves, a bay leaf, a bouquet of fresh herbs, good seasoning of salt and pepper, and two ladles of broth.
Cook the duck this way for half an hour and remove it from the pot.
Strain the broth and remove the fat.
Separately, sauté and brown turnips cut into small chunks or parsnips in the duck's fat.
Once the turnips have browned well, place them in the pot with the duck and in the defatted juice, so they cook together.
When cooking is finished, place the duck on a platter, the turnips around it, and pour the hot sauce over it and the turnips.
For duck with olives: pit the olives, which must be large and sound, and add them to the pot in which the duck cooks in its clean juice ten minutes before serving, so they only give a few boils.
Note: Duck with potatoes, with glazed onions, with vegetable purée, with chard and cabbage is also a tasty dish, but turnips stand out the most.

title: Pavo en Galantina (Turkey Galantine)
description: Prepared with turkey, veal, and ham.

ingredients.name: One cleaned and singed turkey, completely boned raw
ingredients.sourceText: One cleaned and singed turkey, completely boned raw

ingredients.name: Half pound of raw ham, minced
ingredients.sourceText: Half pound of raw ham, minced

ingredients.name: One quarter pound of very fresh bacon, minced
ingredients.sourceText: One quarter pound of very fresh bacon, minced

steps: Bone the turkey completely while raw and separate all its trimmings
Shred the meat from the breasts and legs and place in a bowl, seasoning with salt, pepper, and a few drops of oil
Let the turkey season for a couple of hours
Mince half a pound of veal, half a pound of raw ham, and a quarter pound of very fresh bacon, seasoning well with all spices and moistening with a glass of cognac
Knead this mixture with the shredded turkey meat and incorporate truffles cut like half-pesetas, small cubes of scarlet tongue, and some peeled pistachios
Shape the mixture into a cylindrical form, wrap it tightly in strong linen cloth with ten or twelve turns, and bind securely with string
Place the galantine in a braising pot over coals with a dome-shaped cover on top of the pot
Cook for three hours in concentrated broth that covers it

description: Prepared with turkey and truffles.
steps: Fill the turkey with truffles, increasing the quantity in proportion to the volume of the turkey
Account for the cooking time, as a turkey requires more time than a fattened hen or capon
The turkey may rest with the truffles inside for five or six days in a cool place with no humidity, as dampness would spoil the dish and make the flavor repugnant

title: Pepinillos (Pickled Gherkins)
description: Prepared with cucumbers, wine, and bay leaves.

ingredients.name: Small cucumbers (no larger than a finger)
ingredients.sourceText: Small cucumbers (no larger than a finger)

steps: Clean the gherkins well with a brush and cut off the tip
Place in a tinned iron pot with two handfuls of ground salt, mixing it with them
Leave for twenty-four hours so they release their water
Remove and let drain for a few moments
Return to the same vessel and pour boiling good vinegar over them in sufficient quantity to cover
Cover the vessel and leave for twenty-four hours so they take on a yellowish color
Remove the vinegar and cook it alone over high heat
When it boils vigorously, add the gherkins and stir so they turn green again; four minutes of boiling is sufficient
Remove and place in fresh cold water where they are left to cool

Spread on dry linen to air, and when they have released the water, pack in wide-mouthed glass jars or bottles, arranging them one on top of another, placing here and there some bay leaves and some peppercorns
Pour white vinegar over them in quantity sufficient for the cucumbers to be completely covered, adding two ounces of salt per azumbre of vinegar
Finish the operation by adding oil, which remains on top like that of a small lamp, thus forming a layer that preserves the food from any spoilage

title: Pepinos Preparados (Prepared Cucumbers)
description: Prepared with cucumbers, salt, and water.
steps: Peel the cucumbers and cut into wheels the thickness of a peseta coin
Place in a shallow soup plate
Add plenty of salt as each wheel is arranged
Cover the plate with another plate
Every two hours, hold both plates with both hands, keeping them together, and stand them upright so the water the cucumber releases drains
After eight hours, remove and wash in very fresh water
Let drain and dry
Eat with the dressing desired

title: Pepitoria de gallina á estilo de taberna (Tavern-Style Chicken Pepitoria)
description: Prepared with fat, onions, and mushrooms.
steps: Cut the chickens into pieces
Blanch for 3 minutes in boiling water and drain
Place in a pan with butter, parsley sprigs, saffron, small onions and mushrooms; stew everything together
Add a spoonful of flour and moisten with broth
Season with salt and pepper and cook
Remove the chicken pieces and reduce the sauce
Strain the sauce, dissolve egg yolks in it without letting them cook, and pour over the chicken pieces with lemon juice

title: Pepitoria de Perdices (Partridge Pepitoria)
description: Prepared with partridges, pork, and white wine.
steps: Cut the partridges into four pieces
Brown them over high heat in pork lard, and when very golden, sprinkle with flour
Stir well and season
Moisten with half a quart of water and a glass of the best white wine available, and add very small onions, mushrooms, one clove of garlic and pieces of celery stalks
Cook everything for one hour at low heat
Place the dish on a platter and cover with a large sheet of bacon like a veil
Before serving, keep it in the oven for thirty minutes at medium heat

title: Perdices Encebolladas (Partridges with Onions)
description: Prepared with partridges, onions, and pork.
steps: Clean and prepare the birds
Put pork lard in a pan and sauté one pound of finely chopped onions well with good seasoning, two bay leaves, thyme, parsley and chervil if available
Once the onion is softened, add broth or water until it forms a paste
Scald the partridges over high heat with a little lard in a pan, then add them to the onion mixture
Cook at low heat for about one hour if the partridges are not very tough
Serve them on a platter, covering them with the onion paste that results from this stew

Some serve without further preparation; others pour beaten egg yolks on top; some add chocolate, either beaten on top or one ounce whole inside the partridge when browning it

title: Perdigones a la Inglesa (Young Partridges English Style)
description: Prepared with partridges, salt or pepper or sauce, and oil.

Bathe them in an oil marinade

title: Perdigones Asados (Roasted Young Partridges)
description: Prepared with partridges and bacon.
steps: Truss the young partridges as you would chickens, wrapping them with a thin slice of bacon
Stretch the legs and secure them on the spit or roasting rod so they do not bend, following the figure shown for such birds on page 440
For red partridges, wrap the head and neck very well in thick wet paper so the feathers do not burn

Arrange the bird on a platter with invisible small canes that keep the head upright as if the bird were alive and the body hidden in undergrowth, which is simulated with watercress that completely envelops the roasted meat, well sprinkled with its own juice

title: Perdigones Salteados (Sautéed Young Partridges)
description: Prepared with partridges, butter or lard, and white wine.
steps: Clean and prepare the young partridges without cutting them
Cook them over high heat in butter or lard, turning them frequently so they color evenly
Once cooked, remove them and set aside on a platter, keeping it well covered near the fire
In the same cooking fat, lightly toast a tablespoon of flour
Moisten it with a glass of white wine and a ladle of clean broth
Season with salt and pepper and reduce by half
Add the juice of one whole lemon
Pour this sauce over the young partridges at the moment of serving at the table
